clue.text: Stout aunt's off to church

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or out of order, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S taken as written, letters for shuffling

explanation.surface: A portly aunt sets off for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like a description of the aunt but it is the definition, in its sense of firm and loyal; the possessive S is part of what 'off' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean resolute and steadfast, a synonym for loyal and unwavering.

clue.text: Fire an employee for drinking, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from a job
an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry, something to drink

explanation.surface: A worker is dismissed for boozing on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss is to fire, and the old fortified wine of Shakespeare's Falstaff bears the same name.

clue.text: Off on a course

definitions.meaning: playing at the opponent's ground or course rather than at home

explanation.definitionFit: Absent from home is a synonym of off, and a team playing at the rival's ground plays at that venue rather than at home.

clue.text: It's not always bound to be worn in the boudoir

definitions.text: It's not always bound to be worn in the boudoir

parts.words: It's not always bound to be worn in the boudoir
parts.note: a flimsy bedroom garment, often left loosely tied or open

explanation.surface: Something worn in a lady's bedroom that need not be fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain' (not always bound to be worn) but it means tied up: the garment is often loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, sheer dressing gown worn in a bedroom, typically loosely fastened.

clue.text: Dog or badger

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to pester or harass persistently

explanation.definitionFit: A hunting dog is a canine, and to pester someone relentlessly is the verb sense.

clue.text: Not off on a visit, but ready to make one

parts.note: the opposite of off is on
a call is a short visit

explanation.surface: A doctor not out visiting but available to go out if summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor available to be summoned for a visit is described with this idiom of duty.

clue.text: Agent gets upset over point in veto

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over, above, the next
upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of the agent are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A spy is angry about a disputed point in a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is only a link; 'upset' rearranges AGENT, and 'over' works because this is a down entry, so that piece stands above the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to cancel or nullify it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Well-spoken couple

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to join by a joint

explanation.definitionFit: Fluent speech is the adjective sense, and to connect by joints is the verb sense.

clue.text: Falls in love, but becomes disillusioned

definitions.meaning: gives one's heart away to someone

explanation.definitionFit: Giving away one's heart to a lover and growing discouraged share this idiom.

clue.text: Noise of a dropped brick?

parts.note: dropping a brick is British slang for a blunder, also called a clanger, and a real brick falling would make a loud din

explanation.surface: The sound a brick makes when it falls.
explanation.walkthrough: To drop a brick or drop a clanger is British slang for making an embarrassing blunder; the answer is a ringing din built on that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, continuous ringing din, the sort of racket a heavy object makes falling.

clue.text: Name for stones when placed round an entrance

indicators.note: the word for when is set around the entrance

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: What stones are called when they are set around a gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' looks like a link word but gives letters; 'an' is the link, and 'Name for stones' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These banded chalcedony gemstones are a type of stone, so the plural names them.

clue.text: Harvest genuine support for the church

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits beneath the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
real means genuine

explanation.surface: Gathering crops is a true sign of backing for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for' places REAL beneath CE in this down entry. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain crops such as wheat are harvested, so the word for grain stands for the harvest.

clue.text: Rubbish played on violins

definitions.meaning: bows, the sticks drawn across a fiddle's strings

explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation meaning nonsense, and literally the bows drawn across fiddles.

clue.text: Sailors on a course of medicine?

indicators.note: sailors are on, at, the racecourse, so they follow its name

parts.note: Epsom is a famous English racecourse, home of the Derby
salts are old sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is an English racecourse where the Derby is run; SALTS are sailors. The question mark flags that the definition is a kind of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium sulphate crystals taken as a purgative are a traditional remedy.

clue.text: Clean motor in preparation for a rally

indicators.note: letters being prepared, worked into new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Polishing the car before a motor rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in preparation' rearranges CLEAN MOTOR; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous annual car race starting in Monaco is a well-known motor rally.

clue.text: Restricted places of call

parts.note: small confined kiosks where one makes a telephone call

explanation.surface: Ports where ships may stop only under limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places of call' suggests ports of call; the places are cramped booths for making calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Public kiosks for telephoning are small enclosed spots where one makes calls.

clue.text: Mince pie to include a drug

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the A
to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mince pie laced with a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' shuffles PIE and TO into OPITE, which 'include' A to give the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic derived from opium is a drug.

clue.text: It's not true I was imprisoned by the French

indicators.note: the letter is locked up inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone protests their innocence of being jailed by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is something not true.

clue.text: Leaving as a result of being fired

definitions.text: as a result of being fired
definitions.meaning: what a gun or firework does when fired: exploding

explanation.definitionFit: Departing is one sense; a gun discharging when fired is the other.

clue.text: Frequently coming round on foot?

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Often coming round on foot to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for often, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He sticks up for his employer

definitions.text: He sticks up for his employer

parts.words: He sticks up for his employer
parts.note: not loyal defence but literally pasting up notices for the firm that hires him

explanation.surface: A loyal worker who defends his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticks up for' looks like 'defends' but means pastes up advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who pastes advertising notices on walls and hoardings.

clue.text: Criticises the effects of worn bearings

definitions.meaning: rattling noises from a worn engine part

explanation.definitionFit: Finding fault is one sense; the rattling an engine makes when its parts wear is the other.

clue.text: It's best to back heavyweight individual

parts.note: to second is to back or support
a ton is a heavy weight
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: The best idea is to back a big individual boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better than everyone else means the best, an adjectival idiom.

clue.text: Inert form of chemical

indicators.note: a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An unreactive version of a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: One second inside the current record

parts.note: DC is direct current
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Briefly inside the present record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts I and S within DC, direct current.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat round platter.

clue.text: They support the sovereign, for example — the head of state

parts.note: a sovereign is a gold coin worth one pound, L

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Backers of the monarch, such as the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold coin worth one pound, abbreviated L. 'the head of' takes S from state.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs bear the body's weight, as table supports bear a top.

clue.text: Cyril's odd odes

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the name with its S taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Poems by a man named Cyril are peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of songs or verse, lyrical poems such as odes.

clue.text: I meant to confuse? Never!

indicators.note: to confuse is to muddle, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging, the 'to' included

explanation.surface: Someone denies they intended to bewilder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of the indicator but is fodder: 'confuse' jumbles all eight letters of I MEANT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: On no occasion is the idiom meaning never.

clue.text: Work's returning, employ a partner

indicators.note: coming back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: OP is a musical work (opus), so work's gives OPS
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: Back from work, someone hires a business associate.
explanation.walkthrough: OP (opus) is the usual abbreviation for a musical or literary work, so 'Work's' gives OPS; 'returning' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is a marriage partner.

clue.text: Carries out personal property

explanation.definitionFit: To bring about is the verb sense; one's belongings are the noun sense.
